This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that reports GM volume differences between substance users (heavy drinkers, including a smoking subgroup) and non-drinking controls. The paper provides whole-brain lobar and total neocortical GM comparisons (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, and total cortical GM) between groups, satisfying a whole-brain between-group contrast rather than only isolated ROIs. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/analysis methods are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or non-empirical status).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. The Methods and Results describe whole-brain VBM analyses (ANCOVA, DARTEL normalization, modulation) with reported widespread GM reductions in ADP versus HC (reported in main text and Supporting Information tables), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant demographics (age range, sex matching), substance-use measures (LDH, craving, days abstinent, relapse classification), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; empirical human structural MRI data). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing active heavy drinkers (substance users) with age- and sex-matched light-drinking controls using volumetric measures of gray matter. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise deformation morphometry (ANCOVA and regression maps) comparing HD vs LD, with permutation and cluster-based correction procedures and illustrated t-statistical maps, satisfying whole-brain between-group contrasts. It also provides participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and detailed preprocessing/segmentation and statistical methods. The study is not ROI-only and is not a review. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing alcoholic patients and controls and reports ROI-based gray matter volume analyses in predefined regions of interest (ventromedial PFC, superior frontal gyrus, supplementary motor area, etc.). However, the structural analyses are ROI-only (volumes extracted from ROIs) with no whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls) and I5 (participant demographics and scan details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM results). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only structural results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text presents an empirical MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls using automated hippocampal subfield segmentation (FreeSurfer) and reports subfield volumes (CA2+3, CA4+DG, subiculum) and longitudinal changes. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study comparing GM volume between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criterion I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast) is NOT met: the study focuses on hippocampal subfield ROI segmentation and statistical comparisons of those regions; no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast is reported. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Decision: EXCLUDED due to E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion IDs not met: I3. Exclusion IDs met: E5.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of crack-cocaine (stimulant) users vs controls that reports GM volume differences and provides participant/MRI details (meets I2 and I5). However, the analyses extract regional cortical volumes using predefined ROIs (prefrontal, parietal, temporal, occipital) rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based voxelwise results. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain results (fails I3) and constitutes an ROI-only analysis, which meets exclusion criterion E5. Conclusion: EXCLUDED (E5).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcohol users that reports NAcc gray matter volume differences using FSL-FIRST subcortical segmentation (ROI-based volumetry) and presents multimodal structural and functional results. However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain GM between-group contrasts (e.g., VBM or other whole-brain GM analyses). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence). It does satisfy I2 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details). Full text appears complete.

The study is empirical and uses structural MRI to compare grey-matter-related volumes between heavy-drinking and light-drinking controls, and reports participant demographics and MRI details. However, it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast; analyses are limited to cerebellar lobule volumetry (CERES) and thus are region-of-interest (ROI)-based only. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using VBM (modulated GM segments) to compare alcohol-dependent patients (n=19) with healthy controls (n=20). It performs voxel-wise analyses (one-sample and between-group two-sample t-tests) of an asymmetry index derived from whole-brain GM maps (processed with SPM8/VBM8 and DARTEL) and reports cluster results with peak MNI coordinates and cluster sizes. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (daily intake, dependence duration, abstinence), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results are not limited to ROI-only analyses and voxelwise between-group contrasts are provided (within a right-hemispheric gray matter mask) with appropriate multiple-comparison correction. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore the study meets the review’s requirements for empirical whole-brain voxelwise GM analyses comparing substance users (alcohol) and controls and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing gray matter measures between alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls (meets I2). The paper reports hippocampal GM volume estimates (Hipp/TIV ratio and anterodorsal hippocampal ROI volumes) derived from voxel-based morphometry and uses SPM8 (meets I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts or provide whole-brain coordinate tables/figures for GM differences between substance users and controls. The analyses and results are focused on hippocampal/ROI measures rather than qualifying whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only with no qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-exposed monkeys (N=7) to saline controls (N=7) with voxel-wise morphometry and behavioral/PET correlations. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing substance-exposed vs controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported in figures/tables), I5 (participant age/sex, dosing, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (does NOT report a whole-brain between-group contrast corrected across the entire brain; analyses were confined to a predefined set of ROIs and corrected for the search volume within those ROIs rather than whole-brain inference). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (analyses are effectively ROI-restricted with no qualifying whole-brain results). Additionally, the study uses non-human (vervet monkey) subjects which makes it incompatible with the human-focused meta-analysis scope, reinforcing exclusion. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using deformation-based morphometry to compare recovering alcohol-dependent participants to light-drinking controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise (DBM) between-group contrasts (cross-sectional and longitudinal), including cluster-level results and descriptions of affected GM regions, and provides participant demographics, MRI acquisition, and preprocessing/statistical methods. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for whole-brain GM comparisons and provides adequate methodological and participant detail. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of adolescents with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure vs non-exposed controls that reports ACC volume/area/thickness from Freesurfer parcellation (ROI analyses). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM structural measures between exposed and control groups) and I5 (participant age/sex and MRI details reported). However it does NOT meet I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported); results focus on ACC ROIs only. Therefore E5 applies (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volumes between chronic alcoholic men and healthy controls. The authors measured cortical gray matter (defined across the cortical mantle) and reported between-group contrasts and changes over time, satisfying whole-brain GM comparison requirements rather than an ROI-only approach. Participant demographic and substance-use information (age range, male sex, lifetime alcohol consumption) and MRI acquisition parameters (sequence details, TR/TE, FOV, matrix) are reported; although scanner field strength and voxelwise coordinate tables are not provided, the protocol and regional volumetric results meet the meta-analysis’ acceptable reporting standards and missing single items do not mandate exclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not a review). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Recommended for inclusion for analyses of alcohol-related GM differences.

This article is a narrative/review-style summary of prior MRI studies of prenatal alcohol exposure rather than an original empirical structural MRI study reporting new human voxelwise whole-brain GM between-group contrasts or coordinate tables. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical paper without original human structural MRI data). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM volume differences between substance users and controls), I3 (no original whole-brain between-group GM contrast data presented), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of original results provided in this paper), I5 (as an overview it does not present a single study’s participant-level age/sex, MRI field strength, or preprocessing/statistical software as required for inclusion). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods summary, results, discussion). Thus the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Full text is not available in the provided content (only title, journal metadata, and purchase/access notice). I cannot verify core methods or results. The study appears to examine individuals with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure (exposure in utero) rather than current substance users, so it likely does not meet the review population requirement (studies comparing substance users vs controls). I cannot confirm whether whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts are reported. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete full text preventing assessment of I2 and I3. If full text were available, the in utero exposure population would still likely not meet the meta-analysis focus on substance users, but that cannot be confirmed here.

This study used voxel-based morphometry confined to 13 a priori small-volume templates (small volume correction / masked ROIs) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) voxelwise contrast. Exclusion ID met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM density differences between substance users and controls), I4 (voxelwise results reported with cluster coordinates/statistics), I5 (reports participant/substance-use details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cortical grey matter volumes between methamphetamine-dependent users (n=34) and non-user controls (n=31). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. MRI acquisition (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL for segmentation; SAS for stats) are reported, and participant demographics, age/sex, and substance-use characteristics are detailed. The study performed whole-brain regional analyses by segmenting the entire cortex into six main lobes and 17 subregions (whole-brain coverage) and conducted between-group contrasts (ANCOVA, repeated-measures ANCOVA) comparing GM volumes between users and controls, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Coordinate tables/voxelwise maps are not necessary per I4 since whole-brain ROI-based contrasts are reported in the main text/tables. The study pertains to a stimulant (methamphetamine), matching the meta-analysis objective. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid (SC) users and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain between-group SnPM VBM results (significant clusters in right frontal lobe) and also provides ROI analyses; voxelwise results and coordinates are described/mentioned. Participant demographics (male, ages reported), substance-use characteristics (SC use duration and detected compounds listed in appendix), MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, SnPM) are reported. These satisfy inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; study is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, limitations, appendix). Therefore include for meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users vs. controls.

This is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study of smokers vs never-smokers and reports voxelwise cerebellar coordinates and methodological details, but the analysis is restricted to the cerebellum/brainstem using the SUIT toolbox (i.e., a region-focused, infratentorial mask) rather than a whole-brain GM volume contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only region-of-interest/infratentorial analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I4 (voxelwise result reported as coordinates/figures), I5 (participant and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore exclude under E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volume between substance users (heroin and cocaine use disorder groups) and healthy controls. The paper reports both region-of-interest focused analyses and explicit exploratory whole-brain VBM analyses (noted in the main text and Supplementary Table 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain between-group contrasts. Participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, dcm2niix, etc.) are reported. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical whole-brain GM comparisons and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study directly comparing smokers (nicotine users) and nonsmoking controls. The study used whole-brain coverage via a 1,024-ROI parcellation of the AAL atlas, performed VBM preprocessing (SPM8/VBM8) on 3T data, and applied multivariate classification to discriminate groups. Results include a map of consistent ROIs (N=150) and a table (Table 2) that lists ROIs with MNI center coordinates and sizes, satisfying the requirement that qualifying voxelwise/coordinate results be available. Participant demographics, smoking measures (FTND, CPD, lifetime usage), scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Although the primary analysis is a multivariate classifier rather than a conventional univariate voxelwise t-contrast, the paper provides whole-brain-derived regional results with coordinates and regression analyses relating GMV to smoking measures, which meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4; I5 (reporting details) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter density/volume between cocaine user groups (smoked and insufflated) and matched healthy controls. The authors performed whole-brain voxelwise t-tests (cluster p<.05, extent threshold=50 voxels) and report significant caudate GMd differences associated with behavior; results and coordinates are referenced in main/supplementary materials (tables/figures). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, DPARSF, SPM) are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing young adult recreational cannabis users (n=20) to matched controls (n=20) using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (gray matter density), regional volume, and shape analyses. The paper reports whole-brain VBM contrasts with voxelwise cluster results (Tables/Figures) and provides participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FreeSurfer). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I2,I3,I4,I5). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears to include Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study that reports whole-brain vertexwise analyses (cortical thickness and volumetric measures) comparing children prenatally exposed to cannabis/tobacco vs nonexposed controls. It satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (reports whole-brain between-group GM contrast using vertexwise analyses), I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise results reported in the main text with clusterwise statistics), and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, it does NOT meet inclusion criterion I2 because the comparison is between offspring with prenatal exposure and controls, not between substance-using participants and controls; the meta-analysis objective specifically targets studies of substance users (current/former users) vs controls. No exclusion criteria (e.g., E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) are met. The full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (VBM) comparing heavy smokers (n=16) to matched non-smoker controls and reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses with stereotactic coordinates. The paper provides between-group GM contrasts (VBM) and reports MNI coordinates for GM reductions in bilateral cerebellar tonsil (with small-volume correction) and describes whole-brain thresholding procedures; demographic, substance-use (cigarettes/day, years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, PROBID for SVM) are reported. Voxelwise results are given in-text with coordinates and figures. Although some GM results are reported with small-volume correction, the study conducted whole-brain VBM and provides qualifying voxelwise results; therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E5/E6).

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of methamphetamine (a stimulant) users vs controls that reports whole-brain surface-based group contrasts and provides participant/substance/MRI/software details, it does not assess grey matter volume/density/concentration as specified in inclusion criterion I2. The study uses surface-based cortical thickness measures (FreeSurfer) rather than voxelwise GM volume (e.g., VBM) measures required by I2. Therefore it fails to meet I2 and must be excluded. It does meet I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast), I4 (results reported in main text/figures), and I5 (reports participant age/use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users but it does not include a control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. The analyses are correlational within a single sample and rely on ROI-based VBM/SBM measures of the right insula. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirement for between-group whole-brain GM comparisons. Exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I5 (reporting of participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and software) is met. Inclusion criteria I2 (between-group GM differences vs controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast), and I4 (whole-brain voxelwise results/coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study using T1-weighted data that reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness and voxel-wise VBM comparisons between substance user groups (AUD, OUD, PSU) and healthy controls. The paper provides whole-brain between-group contrasts (controls vs AUD/OUD/PSU and SUD subgroup comparisons) with voxel/vertex-wise results (TFCE, FWE-corrected and also uncorrected thresholds) and details participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM12). It is not an ROI-only study nor a review. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between nicotine-dependent smokers and matched non-smoking controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected VBM results) and provides coordinate/cluster results for left insula and left PFC. Participant demographics, substance-use measures (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, IRG registration, AFNI, etc.) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for GM whole-brain structural comparisons in nicotine users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and TBSS to compare gray matter volume between amphetamine-type stimulant users and controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM) demonstrating reduced gray matter in medial orbitofrontal and dorsal anterior cingulate cortices in experienced users versus low-exposure users and controls. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, TBSS, VBM) are explicitly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study reports only ROI-based subcortical volumetric analyses (seven predefined subcortical ROIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text is available and complete for assessment.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study of alcohol-dependent patients, but it does not include a healthy control group or any whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead, it reports longitudinal (pre–post) within-subject changes and between-treatment (FIR vs routine withdrawal) comparisons among alcohol-dependent participants. Therefore it fails the core inclusion criteria requiring (I2) MRI comparisons between substance users and controls and (I3) at least one whole-brain between-group substance users vs controls contrast. The study does report participant age/sex (male, 18–65), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12/SPM12), satisfying I5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter volumes between occasional amphetamine-type stimulant/cocaine users (N=165) and stimulant-naïve controls (N=48). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses (linear mixed effects model) and whole-brain regressions relating lifetime use to regional GM volume, with coordinates and cluster results described. Methods report participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, FNIRT, FLIRT, AFNI, R). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (PNC sample) comparing adolescent/young adult cannabis users (occasional and frequent) to non-users, reporting measures of gray matter volume and gray matter density. The paper reports whole-brain analyses (global, lobar, and regional/parcelwise contrasts), provides regional maps and analytic code, and applies voxelwise-style testing across the brain (396 comparisons) with FDR correction. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (ANTs, FreeSurfer, R/mgcv) are reported. Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. It is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper, and the provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion: E6 met — this paper is a coordinate-based meta-analysis/network-mapping study synthesizing previously published VBM results and applying normative HCP rs-fMRI; it does not present original empirical between-group structural MRI data from substance users vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an original empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I3 (does not report any new whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls), I4 (while it compiles coordinates from other studies, it does not itself present qualifying voxelwise between-group results), I5 N/A (reporting details relate to aggregated studies rather than original participants). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human MRI study that includes a whole-brain voxelwise VBM analysis comparing grey matter (GM) density between groups of smokers, ex-smokers, and non-smokers (nicotine user group vs controls). The methods describe whole-brain VBM processing and TFCE-corrected group comparisons, and the Results explicitly report VBM findings (no statistically significant GM differences). Participant demographics, substance-use history (pack-years, smoking duration), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FEAT, randomize) are reported. Although the VBM reported null results, the study meets inclusion criteria for whole-brain structural GM comparisons in nicotine users. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analysis or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical human MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses comparing GM across groups (HC, AUD-NCI, ARCI). The manuscript reports methods for structural MRI acquisition (3.0T), preprocessing (CAT12 VBM), and whole-brain statistical testing (FWE-corrected threshold) and provides participant age/sex and substance-use characteristics. Although the VBM results were null (no significant GM differences) and no coordinate tables of significant foci are reported, the study nevertheless performed whole-brain GM comparisons and meets the review inclusion requirements for structural whole-brain GM studies of a substance class (alcohol). Note: because results are null and no coordinates are provided, this study may not contribute coordinate foci to a coordinate-based meta-analysis, but it still satisfies inclusion criteria I2 and I3 and reports the preferred methodological/participant details (I5).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing daily cannabis users to nonusers with voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and FreeSurfer whole-brain GLMs) of gray matter volume/density and shape. The paper reports participant demographics (age/sex counts), substance-use measures, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSLVBM, FreeSurfer, FIRST). Whole-brain contrasts were explicitly performed and reported (though null), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers (nicotine users) and healthy non-smokers using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with MNI coordinates, cluster extents, and FWE-corrected p-values (e.g., decreased GM in left superior/middle frontal gyrus and right orbitofrontal cortex). Participant demographics (age, male-only), substance-use measures (CO, daily cigarettes, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CONN/SPM/CAT12) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for structural GM differences between substance users (nicotine) and controls and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; empirical human data).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volumes between heavy alcohol-using adolescents/young adults and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM between-group contrast (stating no significant clusters on whole-brain analysis) and ROI-corrected voxelwise results with coordinates/figures for regions showing reduced GM in users. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics (AUDIT-C history), MRI field strength (3 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that compares adolescents who initiated heavy/moderate alcohol use to a no/low-drinking control group. The paper reports whole-brain analyses using FreeSurfer cortical parcellation (34 bilateral ROIs covering the cortex) and lobar ROIs with between-group contrasts and multiple-comparison correction (FDR/Bonferroni) identifying regions with steeper gray matter declines in heavy drinkers (e.g., frontal, caudal middle frontal, superior frontal, posterior cingulate). Participant age/sex and detailed substance-use measures are reported; MRI preprocessing software (FreeSurfer) and acquisition procedures are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I3 (whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (GM density) and reporting whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. The Methods describe VBM preprocessing (SPM12/CAT12), MRI field strength (3T), and participant demographics/substance use details; results present whole-brain component maps differentiating AUD vs. controls (ICs) and their anatomical localization. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results presented in figures and localization reported), and I5 (reporting of age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study reporting whole-brain (vertex-wise) cortical analyses and detailed participant/substance/MRI information, it does not report between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls. Instead, it examines continuous associations between adolescent substance-use trajectories and gray matter volume in a community sample. The review requires studies to report whole-brain between-group comparisons of substance users vs controls (I2 and I3). Therefore this study does not meet the key inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

E5: Study reports only region-based volumetric analyses (Freesurfer segmentation of subcortical structures and global brain volumes) and regression/group comparisons, but does not report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast (e.g., VBM or SPM voxelwise results). Inclusion met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers vs controls on GM/brain volumes) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, smoking characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion not met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study that compares gray-matter measures between substance initiators (very early alcohol/tobacco initiators) and controls, satisfying the review’s population and exposure requirements. The paper reports whole-brain surface-based vertex-wise analyses (QDECR) of cortical morphology (volume/thickness/area), in addition to ROI analyses, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and acceptable voxelwise reporting (I4). It provides participant demographics (age/sex), substance use characteristics (initiation and age), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v6.0, QDECR), meeting I5. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; is empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports manual volumetric (ROI) measurements of grey-matter structures (temporal lobe, superior temporal gyrus, hippocampus/amygdala) and DTI voxelwise analyses of FA/ADC (diffusion measures). While it is an empirical MRI study and reports participant demographics and scan parameters (meets I2 and I5), it does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast of grey-matter volume (no VBM or whole-brain GM volume maps). The voxelwise analyses presented are of diffusion metrics (FA/ADC), not GM volume, and the volumetric results are ROI-based rather than whole-brain voxelwise. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (no whole-brain GM contrast). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing MDMA (a stimulant) users and matched controls (meets I2). The paper reports detailed participant demographics, substance-use metrics, MRI field strength and preprocessing/statistical software (meets I5). However, group comparisons are reported using atlas-based region-of-interest (ROI) extractions (Desikan–Killiany cortical ROIs; COBRA subcortical ROIs) and ROI-wise statistics across 42 regions. The manuscript does not present a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast (no voxelwise SPM/VBM statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures of voxelwise results are reported), so it lacks qualifying whole-brain evidence required by I3. Therefore it falls under exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical structural MRI study (English) comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and controls and reports regional volumetric differences using automated subcortical and hippocampal subfield segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Analyses are ROI/subfield based (Freesurfer segmentation and ANCOVA of regional volumes), so it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group GM comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses without qualifying whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (DARTEL-based VBM) comparing smokers and age-matched non-smokers. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs non-smokers) with AlphaSim-corrected voxelwise results and region coordinates/tables referenced, and also reports correlations with lifetime tobacco consumption (pack-years). Participant characteristics (all male, ages 23–40), substance-use measures (cigarettes/day, years, pack-years, light vs heavy groups), MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are described. Thus it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain voxelwise contrasts), I4 (results reported in figures/tables), and I5 (key methodological/participant details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing prescription opioid users to controls and reports participant demographics and MRI/preprocessing details (meets I2 and I5). However, the VBM results presented derive from a priori/functional ROIs (L.NAc and L.vmPFC) extracted from rsFC findings rather than reporting a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E5. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language VBM study of cannabis/tobacco users vs controls (meets I2). It reports voxelwise peak coordinates and figures for group contrasts and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM12) (meets I4 and I5). However, all statistical testing was performed within pre-specified ROIs (bilateral hippocampus, PFC, putamen) using ROI-based FWE correction; no whole-brain between-group GMV contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets the exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This longitudinal MRI study reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness comparisons between adolescents who initiated alcohol use and non-users, identifying a significant cluster (right middle frontal gyrus) with Talairach coordinates and cluster statistics, and also provides whole-brain analyses of other structural measures. Participant ages/sex, substance use characteristics, scanner field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, FSL, SPM) are reported. Although the study uses cortical thickness (surface-based) rather than VBM gray-matter volume per se, it addresses structurally altered grey matter with whole-brain between-group contrasts and supplies coordinate results, satisfying the review objective to identify consistent regions of altered GM between substance users and controls.

Full text is complete. The study is an empirical, English-language MRI study that reports comparisons of grey matter volumes between cannabis users and non-users (I2 satisfied). It provides participant demographics and MRI details (I5 satisfied). However, it does not report whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results (no VBM/whole-brain contrast maps or coordinate tables/figures), so it fails to meet the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I3 not met). It also does not provide coordinate tables or voxelwise figures to satisfy I4. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI/global volumetric results with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it lacks whole-brain/voxelwise between-group GM contrasts (E5).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain VBM and reports voxelwise coordinates and participant demographics/scanner/preprocessing (satisfying I4 and I5). However, it does not include a non-user healthy control group or any contrasts of substance users versus controls; all reported between-group contrasts are among different user groups (alcohol-only vs alcohol+tobacco, alcohol+cannabis, tri-users). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 (must compare substance users to controls) and I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of adolescents comparing cerebellar gray/white matter and CSF trajectories between youths who initiated substantial alcohol use and no/low drinkers. It meets inclusion I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and methodological details). However, the paper performs targeted cerebellar lobular and tissue-segmented regional analyses (SUIT parcellation) rather than reporting at least one whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or whole-brain coordinate results. Therefore it does not meet I3 (whole-brain evidence). Because no whole-brain analyses are provided and the study is effectively ROI/parcellation-based, it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing cannabis users vs non-users. The paper reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (SPM8) with region-level results (including family-wise error correction) and follow-up voxelwise/ROI analyses. Participant characteristics (mean age, familial risk, sex used as covariate), substance use measures (lifetime cannabis, alcohol, cigarettes), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8, DARTEL, SPSS) are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume/density between smokers and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM2; FDR-corrected results) with results presented in tables/figures and describes participant demographics (age/sex), smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Therefore it meets the review inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs. healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The paper reports whole-brain between-group GM contrasts (cross-sectional and longitudinal), cluster- and voxel-level results (FWE-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) with anatomical localization and individual plots; preprocessing/statistics are described (Cat12, SPM12), MRI field strength (1.5T) and participant demographics (age, sex: all male) are reported. It is not ROI-only and is original human MRI data. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a longitudinal imaging study of first-episode schizophrenia patients treated with antipsychotics; it is not a study of substance users versus controls. It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing substance users to non-using controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant age/sex, some substance-use screening details, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain results related to substance use). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (analyses are ROI-based/no qualifying whole-brain results relevant to substance-use contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for not addressing the review population/outcomes.

This is an empirical 7T MRI study of cannabis users vs controls that reports gray matter volume metrics (e.g., FreeSurfer cortical/NAc volumes) and participant demographics, satisfying I2 and I5. However, the paper does not present a whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group contrast of GM volume (instead it reports volume analyses focused on hubs/nodes of corticocerebellar networks and selected ROIs, and reports one significant ROI result: larger left nucleus accumbens). No whole-brain VBM/vertexwise results, tables of coordinates, or whole-brain statistical maps are reported, so it fails I3 (whole-brain evidence) and I4 (voxelwise results not provided). Because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results, exclusion criterion E5 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol users (binge drinkers) and non-binge moderate controls. The manuscript reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group GMV contrasts (BD vs MD) with correction for multiple comparisons and cluster reporting, and provides region clusters/figures/tables. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characterization, MRI field strength (3T Siemens Prisma), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12/DARTEL, AFNI, Bioimage Suite) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets I2, I3, I4, and I5. It is not an ROI-only paper nor a non-empirical article, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter between smokers (nicotine users: current/past) and nonsmokers. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (VBM, SPM2) with regions surviving FWE correction, and provides participant age/sex, smoking definitions, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cigarette smokers (n=44) and matched non-smoker controls (n=44). The paper reports whole‑brain, voxel-wise two-sample t-test contrasts in SPM5/VBM5.1 with cluster-level reporting (thresholds and cluster sizes described) and identifies regions of reduced gray matter in smokers. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (cigarettes/day, years smoking), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. The study is not ROI-only and includes complete core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing older smokers (nicotine users) to matched never-smoker controls (N=39 pairs). The paper reports whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts (SPM2) with cluster results and coordinates described, and authors reran thresholds to confirm robustness. Participant demographics, smoking history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, MATLAB, Stata) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No ROI-only or non-empirical study issues were identified. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) vs controls and reports regional volumetric results using FreeSurfer segmentation (meets I2 and I5). However, the paper reports ROI-based segmentation/volume analyses (subcortical nuclei, lobar WM, corpus callosum) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM volume contrast. No qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain mass-univariate GM results are reported, so it meets Exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore it fails Inclusion I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and I4 (qualifying voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion justified by E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing chronic smokers (n=22) to matched controls using voxel-based morphometry (FSL-VBM) and reporting whole-brain between-group contrasts. The paper reports significant reductions in gray matter density in dlPFC and insula/operculum in smokers (with statistics), describes participant age/sex and smoking characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software. Thus it satisfies the review’s criteria for inclusion and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing smokers (n=3,292) vs non-smokers (n=6,842) that reports differences in grey matter (global GM, lobar regions, and AD-relevant regions including hippocampus and precuneus) derived from whole-brain automated segmentation (FastSurfer analysis of 96 regional volumes and ICV-adjusted comparisons). The paper provides participant demographics (age range, sex), smoking characteristics (pack-years), MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FastSurfer, nnU-Net, sklearn/SciPy). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and presents whole-brain between-group contrasts (ICV-adjusted volumetric comparisons and regression analyses). Therefore it satisfies I2 and I3 and meets I5 (reporting key methodological/participant details). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of nicotine (smoking) users vs controls (UK Biobank, n=33,293) assessing grey matter volume differences across the whole brain. The manuscript reports total and regional GMV comparisons covering 166 atlas-defined ROIs spanning the whole brain, with appropriate preprocessing (CAT12), MRI field strength (3T), participant demographics (age, sex), and statistical analyses including multiple-comparison corrections and supplementary tables of regional results. Although analyses were region-based (AAL3 parcellation) rather than voxelwise SPM coordinates, they provide whole-brain between-group contrasts and regional results in tables/supplementary material, meeting the review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; supplementary tables are referenced for regional findings. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as a whole-brain structural MRI comparison of substance (nicotine) users vs controls.

This study is excluded because it does not report whole-brain GM comparisons between substance users and non-using controls. Although it is an empirical, English-language MRI study using GMV measures and whole-brain multimodal spatial maps, the between-group contrasts are current smokers versus long-term ex-smokers (both groups with lifetime tobacco exposure) rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Thus inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls) are not met. The full text is complete and reports whole-brain spatial component maps (satisfying I4). No exclusion criteria (E5 ROI-only or E6 non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of alcohol users vs healthy controls that reports whole-brain voxelwise GM volume analyses (voxel-based ANCOVAs using SPM12 on 3T T1-weighted images) and presents between-group contrasts (AUD vs HC and AUD-subgroup contrasts) with cluster-level correction. Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results (significant GM volume differences) are reported in the main text/figures and therefore satisfy whole-brain coordinate/voxelwise reporting. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for alcohol-related GM comparisons.

This is an empirical English MRI study of methamphetamine (a stimulant) vs controls reporting whole-brain cortical thickness reductions and participant/MRI details. However, the meta-analysis requires studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences (e.g., volume, density, or concentration) (I2), and whole-brain between-group contrasts must compare GM volume (I3). This study reports cortical thickness (morphometric surface-based measure), not GM volume/density/concentration; therefore it does not meet I2 (and consequently I3 as specified). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reporting participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing). Inclusion criteria not met: I2, I3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol dependence using FreeSurfer-derived regional measures across the whole cortex and subcortex (meets I2). It reports participant/sample details and preprocessing (FreeSurfer 5.3, QC protocols) (meets I5). However, the study does not present whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate tables/figures of voxelwise results comparing GM volume/density (it uses ROI/parcellation measures and machine-learning feature importance rather than voxelwise statistical maps). Therefore it fails the required whole-brain evidence criterion (I3) and does not provide voxelwise coordinate results (I4). This matches exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI/parcellation analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Although this is an empirical, English-language MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports whole-brain vertex-wise maps and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software, it does NOT assess grey matter (GM) volume/density/concentration. The primary outcome is intracortical myelin (ICM) signal (T1/PD ratio mapping), not GM volume or voxel-based morphometry contrasts. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I3 (reports at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxelwise results/maps reported) and I5 (reporting of age/sex, substance characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5, E6) apply. Decision: EXCLUDED for not reporting GM volume differences required by the review.

E5: The study conducts ROI-based cortical thickness analyses (dorsal prefrontal cortex) and does not report whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain GM volume between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports participant/sample characteristics and MRI preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess GM volume/density/concentration between substance users and controls using VBM-style measures), I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast reported), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise whole-brain coordinates/contrast for GM volume). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter (cortical thickness and gray matter density) between cannabis-dependent users and matched controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel/vertex-wise between-group contrasts (voxelwise/vertex-wise analyses identifying a significant precuneus cluster with MNI coordinates and cluster statistics), and parcel-wise (Desikan−Killany) analyses of gray matter differences. Participant demographics and substance-use characteristics, MRI acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (Freesurfer, SPM, DARTEL, PALM/FSL randomise) are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing adults with cocaine use disorder (stimulant class) to healthy controls. It reports whole-brain vertex-wise comparisons of cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) with family-wise error correction and ROI-based analyses, and provides voxel/vertex-level results in figures/tables. Participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, MATLAB) are reported. Although the primary morphometric measure is cortical thickness rather than VBM-based GM volume/density, it qualifies as grey-matter structural alteration relevant to the review objective. Therefore the study meets the required criteria for inclusion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heavy-drinking adolescents to non-drinking controls with longitudinal within-subject measurements. The paper reports gray matter volume differences across the whole neocortex and lobar regions using atlas-based whole-brain parcellation (not limited to single small ROIs), demonstrating group-by-age trajectory differences in frontal and temporal cortical volumes. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (e.g., SRI24 atlas, FSL FAST, lme4 in R) are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets criteria for inclusion in a meta-analysis seeking whole-brain GM volume differences between substance users (alcohol) and controls.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcoholics vs controls measuring regional brain volumes (meets I2). Participant demographics and MRI details are reported (meets I5). However, the study uses semi-automated, observer-assisted regional/ROI volumetric analyses of predefined reward and comparison regions and reports regionwise/group comparisons—not whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of methamphetamine users vs controls that reports cortical thickness (surface-based morphometry) and structural covariance network findings, but it does not report grey matter volume, density, or concentration contrasts (voxelwise or volumetric GM results) required by the review inclusion criterion I2. It performs ROI-based cortical thickness analyses using the Desikan–Killiany parcellation rather than whole-brain voxelwise GM volume contrasts; therefore it fails to meet I2 and I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results). The paper does report participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software (satisfies I5). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I2, I3 (and I4 not applicable). Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This study is an empirical, full-text structural MRI paper but it assesses cortical thickness and structural covariance networks using ROI-based cortical thickness measures (Desikan atlas), not grey matter (GM) volume/density/concentration voxelwise contrasts required by the review. It does not report whole-brain voxelwise GM volume between-group contrasts comparing substance users to controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I2 (GM volume measure) and I3 (whole-brain GM volume contrast). It does report participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI preprocessing and software (satisfies I5). Because the analyses are ROI/parcellation-based and lack qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM volume results, it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results).

The study is an empirical structural MRI paper but reports surface-based morphometric measures (cortical thickness, gyrification index, sulcal depth, fractal dimension) and morphological network analyses rather than grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant demographics, substance use details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not assess GM volume/density/concentration) and I3 (does not provide a whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume). No exclusion criteria from the list (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis use disorder (CUD) participants to non-users using whole-brain morphometric analyses. The authors report cortical thickness, cortical surface area (68 cortical parcels from Desikan–Killiany), subcortical and cerebellar volumes (14 subcortical regions) derived from Freesurfer on 3T data, and present between-group contrasts (reporting null and region-wise results). Participant demographics, scanner field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are described. The study therefore meets: I2 (empirical MRI GM differences), I3 (whole-brain between-group morphometry across the cortex and subcortex), I4 (results reported in text/tables/figures), and I5 (participant and MRI/preprocessing details). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and complete for screening.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing heroin (opioid) users and healthy controls using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (VBM). The paper reports widespread GM atrophy in heroin abusers versus controls, details voxelwise ANOVA results, and provides coordinates/clusters and subsequent ROI-based connectivity analyses. Participant characteristics (age, sex), substance-use criteria, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing (SPM8, DARTEL) and statistical software are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts), I4 (voxelwise results reported in text/tables/figures), and I5 (participant and MRI methodological details provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of alcohol use disorder (relevant drug class). It reports whole-brain voxel-wise (GMD via VBM) and vertex-wise (cortical thickness via FreeSurfer) between-group contrasts (AUD vs. healthy controls) with corrected statistics and cluster/vertex results presented in figures/tables. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), acquisition parameters, preprocessing and statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.3, SPM12, DARTEL, FSL PALM) and substance-use measures are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is a Mendelian randomization and multiomics analysis using GWAS summary data linking genetically predicted brain structure to alcohol use. It is not an empirical case-control structural MRI study comparing substance users versus controls and does not report whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts of substance users vs controls. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing amphetamine-dependent patients (n=40) to healthy controls (n=40) using whole-brain, vertex-wise cortical thickness analysis. The paper reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (multiple contrasts vs controls), visualizes results across the cortical mantle, and applies multiple-comparison correction (FDR). Participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer) are reported. Although the metric is cortical thickness rather than VBM volume/density, cortical thickness is a widely accepted grey-matter structural measure aligned with the meta-analysis objective of identifying structural GM alterations. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing substance-dependent individuals (SDI) and controls using surface-based morphometry (FreeSurfer) reporting cortical volume and thickness differences (I2). The paper reports vertex-wise whole-brain analyses (group and group-by-sex contrasts) for thickness and volume, with results described and mapped (whole-brain between-group contrasts present, satisfying I3 and I4). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SPSS) are reported (I5). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter between 20 male alcohol-dependent patients and 20 controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group analyses (SPM2) with regional results (clusters/regions identified) and correlational analyses with substance-use measures and neuropsychological performance. Key methodological details are provided (3.0T scanner, preprocessing software: ANALYZE, BET, FAST, SPM2; participant sex and age-matched controls; drinking-history measures). The study is not ROI-only and provides original human MRI data. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it reports cortical thickness (surface-based morphometry) differences rather than the grey matter volume/density/concentration measures required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (voxel/vertex-wise results reported with coordinates/figures) and I5 (participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, preprocessing software reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (study does not assess GM volume/density/concentration) and I3 (while a whole-brain between-group contrast is reported, it assesses cortical thickness rather than GM volume as required). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical MRI study of 94 men with severe alcohol use disorder, reporting cortical thickness correlations with depressive and anxiety symptoms. However, it does not include a healthy control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users versus controls of grey matter volume/density. The meta-analysis requires studies that assess GM volume differences between substance users and controls (I2) and report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast (I3). While the paper reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistics (FreeSurfer/Qdec and Monte Carlo correction), satisfying I5, it fails to meet I2 and I3. No exclusion criteria (E5 ROI-only; E6 non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter concentration between MDMA (Ecstasy) polydrug users and non-MDMA controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (SPM results) with both corrected and uncorrected thresholds and describes affected regional coordinates/areas. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM99, VBM) are reported. MDMA is a substituted amphetamine and falls within the stimulants class relevant to the review objective. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of cigarette smokers but it does not include a between-group comparison of substance users versus controls. The analyses examine within-group associations (insula cortical thickness correlated with craving) and focus on a predefined insula region rather than reporting whole-brain between-group GM contrasts. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for studies comparing GM volume/density between users and controls or providing whole-brain voxelwise between-group results.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of cocaine users (a stimulant class) reporting cortical thickness differences (FreeSurfer, 3T scanner) and participant demographics and preprocessing software. However, the imaging analysis is limited to ROI-based cortical thickness measures (MFG, IFG, lOFG, SFG, pericalcarine) and a global mean cortical-thickness metric; the paper does not present a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain between-group contrast or coordinate-based whole-brain results. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I5 but does not meet I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast). It thus falls under exclusion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol-dependent patients with healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (VBM results reported with whole-brain FWE correction, figures, and tables of regional findings) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol use that compares binge-drinking (BD) subjects and healthy controls and reports ROI-based GM volume and other morphometric differences using a Desikan–Killiany atlas and JIVE component analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM morphometry differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software are reported). However, the study does not report any voxelwise whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts or provide coordinate-based whole-brain results; analyses are ROI-based structural covariance/component analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise GM contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and does not meet I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical English-language human MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to healthy controls using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reporting between-group GM volume differences. The paper presents whole-brain 2-sample t-test results (alcoholics vs controls) with reported clusters, peak T-values and MNI coordinates, and figures describing GM deficits. Participant demographics (n, sex distribution), substance-use history, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (VBM5/SPM5, TBM methods) are reported. Therefore it meets the review objective of identifying GM differences in substance users (alcohol) vs controls and satisfies inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study of alcohol use disorder (AUD) patients vs healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry (VBM). It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (two-sample t-tests), voxelwise correlations, conjunction analyses, and refers to tables/figures with coordinates. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT12, DARTEL, TFCE) are reported. The study directly addresses the review objective for the alcohol pharmacological class and provides qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete.

This study is an empirical English structural MRI study that reports GM-related measures (satisfies I2) and provides participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details (satisfies I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrasts or VBM-style whole-brain GM results: analyses are global cortical GM/CSF and ROI/subcortical segmentation (FIRST) with region-wise statistics. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only ROI/subcortical and global measures with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant users) to healthy controls and reports necessary participant and MRI details. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study reporting GM differences) and I5 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software). However, the paper does not report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrasts of substance users vs controls: group comparisons were conducted using an ROI-based approach with small-volume correction (SVC) and no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM results are presented. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criterion I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Exclusion reason summary: E5 met; I2 and I5 met; I3 not met.

Exclusion: E5 (ROI-only / no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results). This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI paper reporting cortical thickness differences between adolescent marijuana+alcohol users and controls using FreeSurfer parcellation-based regional thickness measures across 34 cortical regions. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant age range, sex distribution, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3.0 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer, SPSS) are reported).
