Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (study does not assess grey matter volume/density/concentration; it reports cortical thickness, a different morphometric metric) and I3 (does not report whole-brain voxelwise/volume-based GM between-group contrasts required by the meta-analysis). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to GM volume voxelwise whole-brain results.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain comparison of substance users versus non-using controls in GM volume. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (study reports participant/sample characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.3/QDEC)). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (does not assess GM volume/density/concentration differences between substance users and controls; instead compares early- vs late-onset cannabis users), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls). Exclusion criteria met: none (E5 and E6 do not apply). The study reports surface-based cortical measures (thickness, gray–white contrast, gyrification) within user subgroups rather than voxelwise GM volume comparisons against controls; therefore it does not qualify for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM study of cocaine users vs controls (meets I2). It reports whole-brain voxelwise regression results (within the cocaine group) with figures/tables (I4) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software details (I5). However, the paper does not report a whole-brain between-group (substance users vs controls) voxelwise contrast of GM volume; comparisons to controls are performed post-hoc on extracted ROIs (Welch t-tests), not as a whole-brain voxelwise user-vs-control contrast. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I3 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) explicitly apply, but exclusion is due to missing I3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients (n=20) and matched healthy controls (n=20). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-tests (SPM8 with DARTEL) with FWE-corrected thresholds and describes peak clusters/figures (i.e., whole-brain coordinate/cluster results). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (DSM-IV diagnosis, abstinence duration, MAST, lifetime intake), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study reports hippocampal volume differences (ROI-based hippocampal morphometry) between alcohol-dependent individuals and controls but does not present a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain GM between-group contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) and I5 (reporting of participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and analysis software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because study reports only region-of-interest (insula) analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM volume/density results or extractable voxelwise coordinates. Exclusion ID met: E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study reports cortical thickness rather than GM volume/density measures as specified), I3 (no reported whole-brain between-group contrast with extractable GM differences between substance users and controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise coordinates/results available). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Exclusion E5: The study does not present a qualifying whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume (voxelwise/vertexwise or coordinate-based results). Although it is an empirical MRI study of methamphetamine users vs controls and reports cortical gray-matter thickness and subcortical volumes (meets I2) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software (meets I5), the analyses reported are global mean and selected regional (ROI/post-hoc regional) comparisons and correlations rather than whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise between-group GM volume contrasts required by I3. Therefore it must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical, full-text MRI study reporting whole-brain VBM and SBM analyses and detailed participant/MRI methods; however, it does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users versus controls. Analyses use AUDIT scores as a continuous predictor and report within-sample and within-age-group regressions rather than a direct users vs controls comparison. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I2 and I3. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language human structural MRI study comparing grey matter between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using whole-brain Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM). The manuscript reports voxelwise between-group contrasts, thresholding, and peak voxel MNI coordinates; it presents regions of significant volume decreases in alcoholics and describes regression analyses relating volume/ADC to memory. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2, Brainvisa) are provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison), I3 (whole-brain between-group GM contrast), I4 (voxelwise results reported with coordinates/figures), and I5 (reporting of age/sex/use characteristics and MRI/method details). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing individuals with prenatal alcohol exposure/FASD to controls and reports multiple grey-matter measures (cortical grey matter volume, regional/deep grey matter volumes, and cortical thickness). Analyses used whole-cortex surface-based thickness measures (40,962 vertices/hemisphere, then AAL parcellation) and whole-brain automated segmentation (Freesurfer) to test group differences across the brain, and participant age/sex, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Results include whole-brain regional comparisons (volumes and cortical thickness) between FASD and controls; this is not an ROI-only study. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for grey-matter whole-brain comparisons for alcohol exposure studies.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and age-/gender-matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (One-Way ANCOVA and post-hoc comparisons; cluster-level FWE-corrected results) with supplemental tables referenced for detailed results. Participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM12) are reported. The study therefore meets the review objective (alcohol users vs controls) and satisfies inclusion criteria for empirical MRI GM volume comparisons with whole-brain voxelwise results. It is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary material referenced).

Exclusion (E5) met: the study’s VBM analyses are reported as region-of-interest (ROI) analyses based on AAL templates (left lateral frontal, parietal, temporal lobes and hippocampus) rather than reporting a qualifying whole‑brain between-group contrast of substance users (AUD) vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing GM volume/density between substance users and controls) and I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8)). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrast provided). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion, conclusions present). Therefore excluded under E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing methamphetamine-dependent participants to drug-naïve controls (between-group whole-brain contrasts reported) and a longitudinal within-group comparison. The paper reports whole-brain VBM results (thresholds, cluster correction) and describes affected regions; methods include participant age/sex, substance use history, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not non-empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of stimulants.

This is an empirical structural MRI study (cortical thickness) including a smoker (nicotine) group, so I2 is met, and participant/MRI details are reported (I5 met). However, the study used a predefined set of 15 ROIs (Desikan–Killiany–Tourville atlas) and reports ROI-based cortical thickness analyses rather than at least one whole-brain voxelwise/whole-brain GM volume contrast. It does not present qualifying whole-brain between-group GM volume results or coordinate tables/figures for whole-brain VBM contrasts. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing cocaine users (stimulant class) and non-drug-using controls. It reports cortical volume (CV) measures (in addition to cortical thickness and surface area), and tests between-group differences. The authors performed a whole-brain analysis using Freesurfer QDEC (reported as not yielding significant effects outside ROIs), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain between-group contrast. Participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.0, QDEC) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and is original empirical data. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (FreeSurfer cortical morphometry) comparing polysubstance users and alcohol-dependent participants to controls, and it reports participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (4T), and preprocessing/statistical software. However, the analyses are ROI-based (predefined cortical parcellations and targeted ROI ANCOVAs for ACC, DPFC, OFC, insula) and the paper does not report whole-brain voxelwise or other whole-brain between-group GM contrasts. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain evidence inclusion criterion and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study).

This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM study reporting voxelwise whole-brain results within a sample of 39 heavy drinking smokers. However, it does NOT include a control group nor report any whole-brain between-group contrasts comparing substance users to healthy controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I2 (must assess GM differences between substance users and controls) and I3 (must report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (voxelwise results are reported in the main text/figures) and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software are reported). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter between 30 codeine-containing cough syrup (CCS) users and 30 matched controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts (ANCOVA, corrected p<0.05) with coordinates and cluster sizes for decreased GM in bilateral vmPFC, and links these findings to clinical measures. MRI field strength (1.5T) and preprocessing/software (VBM8/SPM8) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. As CCS is an opioid-containing substance, this study addresses the opioid class for the review and meets inclusion criteria I2–I5. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing college-aged binge drinkers (alcohol users) to matched healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (cluster extent threshold corrected) with coordinates and figures, and also presents SVC results; results and coordinates are clearly available. Participant characteristics (age range/adult status, gender matching), substance use characterization (binge criteria, AUDIT scores), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Tim Trio), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL, smoothing) are reported. The study is not ROI-only and contains full article sections (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between adolescents with alcohol use disorder (substance users) and matched healthy controls. Whole-brain between-group analyses (ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) are reported, with results presented in tables and supplemental materials (coordinates/unorrected and FWE-corrected findings). Participant demographics, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T Siemens), acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM) are provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (VBM/SBM) comparing chronic alcohol consumers (n=50) to matched controls (n=43) with whole-brain voxel-wise analyses reporting regional gray matter volume differences. Participants’ ages and sex (all male) are provided; MRI field strength (3.0 T) and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, FSL) are reported. Voxel-wise whole-brain contrasts and region-level results are described (with tables/figures referenced). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between nicotine-dependent cigarette smokers (n=80) and matched non-smoking controls (n=80). The manuscript reports whole-brain between-group analyses (2×2 factorial, random-field cluster-size testing, whole-brain FWE cluster correction) with reported clusters/figures and coordinates. Participant demographics, smoking characteristics (pack-years, FTND, cigarettes/day), MRI field strength (Siemens 3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria (E5: ROI-only; E6: non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical structural MRI study (FreeSurfer-derived regional volume/thickness) comparing alcohol dependent individuals (n=60) and controls (n=49), so it meets I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons) and I5 (participant and MRI details reported). However, the study used an ROI-based morphometric approach (insula and ACC ROIs from the Destrieux atlas) and reports ROI volumetric/thickness comparisons and correlations; no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast (with coordinates or voxelwise results) is reported. Therefore it does not meet I3 (whole-brain evidence) and falls under exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Exclusion ID: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I2, I5. Inclusion ID not met: I3.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study of adolescent alcohol use that reports region-of-interest analyses using FreeSurfer parcellation and linear mixed models, and provides participant age/sex, scanner (3T), and preprocessing software. However, the paper does not report any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group contrasts of substance users versus controls; analyses focused on a priori ROIs and continuous alcohol-index associations and co-twin comparisons. Therefore it fails the review’s requirement for whole-brain between-group GM contrasts (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only, no qualifying whole-brain results). Included criteria met: I5. Included criteria not met: I3 (and not clearly I2 as a classic between-group users vs controls contrast).

Excluded because the study reports voxel-based morphometry results restricted to a predefined set of nine ROIs (ROI-masked VBM) and presents significant group differences only within these ROIs rather than reporting an unrestricted whole-brain between-group contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM differences) and I5 (participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistics reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no clear whole-brain between-group contrast/results). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of prenatal cocaine-exposed children vs non-exposed controls that reports regional (atlas-derived) volumes (cortical and subcortical) using FreeSurfer. However, it does not present whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results typical for voxelwise GM analyses. Participants are prenatally exposed children rather than substance users themselves. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria: I2 (study does not compare substance users vs controls in the sense of users themselves) and I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM contrast). It does, however, report participant demographics and MRI details (I5). Exclusion criterion E5 applies because the study reports only regional/ROI volume analyses without qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a longitudinal structural MRI study of individuals with cocaine use disorder undergoing treatment (pre-post within-subject comparisons) and does not include any between-group comparisons of substance users versus healthy controls. Therefore it does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for studies that assess grey matter differences between substance users and controls. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reporting of participant/treatment/MRI/preprocessing details). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (empirical MRI study comparing GM between substance users and controls), I3 (at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of users vs controls), I4 (not applicable because no between-group voxelwise results are reported). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not meet E5 or E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between cigarette smokers (heavy and light) and never smokers using voxel-based morphometry. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (voxel p<0.001, cluster p<0.05 FWE) with reported clusters and post-hoc tests, and provides participant demographics, smoking characteristics (FTND, years of smoking), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study, but it reports cortical thickness ROI analyses confined to 11 bilateral frontal regions (Desikan–Killiany atlas) rather than whole-brain voxelwise/volume-based between-group GM contrasts. Therefore it violates the review’s requirement for whole-brain GM volume/density/concentration comparisons. Exclusion ID met: E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (participant age/sex and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study reports cortical thickness, not the GM volume/density/concentration measures specified), I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts reported), I4 (no voxelwise whole-brain coordinates/results provided). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between poly-drug users (PUD) and healthy controls. The paper reports a whole-brain VBM analysis (TFCE permutation testing) of GMV between groups (null results reported), and provides participant demographics (age, all-male sample), substance use characteristics (diagnosis, duration, maintenance/abstinence, medication), MRI field strength (3T Siemens Skyra), and preprocessing/statistical software (MRtrix, FSL, SPM12, CAT12). Thus it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for empirical whole-brain GM comparisons and reports necessary methodological details. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs healthy controls reporting whole-brain volumetric and cortical thickness comparisons. The paper presents comprehensive whole-brain automated segmentation results (volBrain) including global, lobar, subcortical, and regional cortical measures and between-group contrasts (with statistics and effect sizes) that cover the whole brain; regional results and correlations are reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (volBrain, JASP/SPSS/Python) are provided. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analyses or non-empirical type) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing chronic cannabis users (n=11) to matched controls (n=13). The paper reports whole-brain between-group analyses (unmodulated GM: no whole-brain differences reported) and voxelwise ROI results with stereotactic coordinates for hippocampal clusters (modulated and unmodulated data), satisfying the requirement for voxelwise results (coordinates and figures reported). Participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL) are reported. Although key findings are hippocampal and small-volume-corrected, whole-brain analyses were performed and voxelwise results are available. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol-dependent males vs healthy controls (alcohol is a target drug class). It uses whole-brain surface-based morphometry to assess cortical thickness and reports a whole-brain between-group contrast with coordinates (left postcentral gyrus, x=-48,y=-12,z=31) and cluster-level results. MRI field strength (3T) and preprocessing/statistical software (CAT12, SPM12, CONN) are reported, and participant/substance characteristics (age, sex, AUDIT/BMAST scores, drinking duration) are provided. Although the measure is cortical thickness (surface-based) rather than VBM volume/density, it is a whole-brain grey-matter structural metric relevant to the meta-analysis objective of identifying structurally altered GM regions. The study is empirical and not ROI-only, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing chronic nicotine users (smokers) to non-smoker controls and to subgroups (early- vs late-onset). The paper reports voxel-wise two-sample t-tests and whole-brain voxel-wise regression analyses (SPM12 VBM) with cluster-level correction and provides MNI coordinates and figures/tables of significant GM/WM clusters (insula, ACC, thalamus, corpus callosum, etc.). MRI field strength (Siemens 3T Prisma-FIT), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM12, CAT), and participant demographics/ substance-use measures are reported. Although analyses were limited in scope to a priori ROIs (masked voxelwise analyses), results are reported as voxelwise whole-brain contrasts with coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise evidence. Therefore inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5 are met.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing heavy smokers and non-smokers and reports regional grey-matter-related measures (cortical thickness) using 3.0T MRI and FreeSurfer (satisfies I2 and I5). However, the study does not report whole-brain voxelwise GM volume/density contrasts or whole-brain coordinate tables; analyses focus on the insula (subregional ROI/parcellation using the Destrieux atlas). Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (whole-brain GM volume contrast). Exclusion criteria applied: E5. Result: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical English MRI study comparing SUD participants and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, scanner types, preprocessing and software (meets I5). However the study reports analyses restricted to a pre-selected set of 24 ROIs (FreeSurfer-derived regional volumes) rather than a whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain mass-univariate between-group contrast. The review’s requirement for whole-brain evidence (I3) is not met, and the study therefore falls under exclusion E5 (reports only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study assessing grey matter volume differences between substance users and controls (I2 met) and it reports participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strengths and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer) (I5 met). However, the analyses are based on a predefined set of 24 ROIs and ROI-based, atlas-parcellation comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts or coordinate-based voxelwise results; no whole-brain voxelwise contrast tables of coordinates or peak coordinates are provided. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria I3 (whole-brain between-group contrast) and I4 (voxelwise/coordinate results available) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing heavy cannabis users (n=20) to healthy controls (n=22) that reports cortical volume (a GM volume metric) along with cortical thickness and surface area. The study performed whole-brain vertex-wise analyses using FreeSurfer with general linear models and reports clusters surviving multiple-comparison correction; cluster sizes and MNI coordinates are noted in the text/tables. Participant ages are reported and preprocessing/statistical software are described (FreeSurfer, SimNIBS, mri_glmfit, R). While MRI field strength and some substance-use detail depth are not fully described in the excerpt, the inclusion guidance states missing such items alone should not exclude the study. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion sections, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM volume comparisons for cannabis users vs controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and matched controls (meets I2). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with familywise-error cluster correction and presents results in figures and tables (meets I3 and I4). Participant age/sex, substance-use metrics, MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing (SPM8 DARTEL VBM) and statistical software (AFNI) are reported (meets I5). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not an ROI-only study nor a non-empirical paper. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical, English-language human MRI study comparing detoxified alcohol-dependent patients to matched healthy controls using whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness (surface-based) analysis. It reports whole-brain between-group contrasts (significant left superior frontal cluster) after correcting for multiple comparisons, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), acquisition parameters, and preprocessing/statistical methods. Cortical thickness is a valid grey-matter structural metric relevant to the review objective of structurally altered GM between substance users and controls (alcohol is within the targeted drug classes). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not perform a between-group case-control comparison of substance users vs. controls and reports no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports participant age/sex and MRI/preprocessing/statistical details). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I2 (does not compare substance users vs controls for GM differences), I3 (no whole-brain between-group contrasts of users vs controls), I4 (no qualifying voxelwise between-group results reported). The full text is complete and contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain between-group comparisons and is excluded.

This is an empirical human MRI VBM study of methamphetamine-dependent individuals vs. controls (stimulant class) that reports gray matter differences. However, the VBM analysis results reported are based on extraction of average modulated gray matter volumes from a predefined set of 70 ROIs and subsequent ROI-based analyses (exploratory correlations and group comparisons for the thalamic LD). The full text does not report voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts (no whole-brain statistical maps, cluster coordinates, or coordinate tables are provided). Therefore the study reports only ROI-based results and does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise comparisons required by the review. Exclusion per E5 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results).

This VBM study of alcohol use disorder is empirical, in English, reports GM volume differences between substance users and controls (meets I2) and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software details (meets I5). However, the VBM analysis was conducted within predefined network ROI/mask regions (salience, default mode, executive control) and the authors state that "GM volumes of the ROIs were compared" and report results within those masks. There is no clear whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast reported; results are restricted to ROI/mask-based comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (ROI-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast). Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This is an original, English-language empirical VBM study comparing grey matter volume between nicotine users (young male smokers; n=26) and matched controls (n=26). It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts using SPM8/VBM8 with FWE correction (p<0.05) identifying decreased GM in left ACC and increased GM in left putamen. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics (CPD, pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for studies of structural GM differences in substance (nicotine) users versus controls.

This study is an empirical, English-language MRI study that reports complete participant details (age/sex), MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/software (FreeSurfer) satisfying I5. However, the primary neuroimaging outcome is cortical thickness measured with FreeSurfer across 148 atlas regions (region-wise cortical thickness), not grey matter volume/density/concentration (e.g., VBM) as required by I2. The analyses are region-based (parcellation) rather than voxelwise whole-brain GM volume contrasts and do not provide qualifying voxelwise GM volume coordinates or maps; therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI/region-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain GM volume results). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (GM volume measures) and I3 (a whole-brain GM volume between-group voxelwise contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter-related regional volumes between alcohol-dependent subjects and controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (3T), and analysis software (meets I5). However, the paper performs segmentation-based regional volumetry (predefined bilateral ROIs such as cortex, hippocampus, thalamus, etc.) and reports region-wise volume comparisons rather than any whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast or coordinate-based results. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain/voxelwise GM evidence required for inclusion and must be excluded under E5 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that compares participants with cocaine use (including HIV−/CU+ and HIV+/CU+) to controls (HIV−/CU−). The paper reports whole-brain surface-based morphometric analyses (cortical thickness, cortical volume, sulcal depth, surface area) and group contrasts across networks, with univariate follow-up tests showing reduced cortical thickness in visual and frontoparietal networks and sulcal depth alterations in sensorimotor networks in user/comorbid groups. Participant demographics (age, sex), substance-use grouping (CU status), MRI-based measures, and statistical methods are reported; detailed methods are in supplements but core analyses and results (whole-brain morphometry comparisons between substance users and controls) are present in the full text. The study is not ROI-only and contains original human structural MRI data relevant to stimulants (cocaine). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2 and I3, and reports participant and methods details (I5).

This study is empirical and reports surface-based cortical thickness differences between adolescent binge drinkers and controls using FreeSurfer, and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I5). However, it does not report GM volume/density/concentration voxelwise contrasts (cortical thickness is a distinct morphometric measure rather than the GM volume/density outcomes specified in I2), and primary analyses are regional parcellation (ROI) based with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM volume results to include (thus E5 applies and I2 and I3 are not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls (meets I2) and reports participant demographics and MRI details (meets I5). However, all reported analyses focus on the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) volumes and cortical thickness (ROI/manual tracing and OFC-focused FreeSurfer measures) and no whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain between-group GM contrasts are reported. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I3) and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only study). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3. Exclusion criteria met: E5.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences between alcohol-dependent users and controls via global GM ratio) and I5 (reports participant age/sex/ substance use characteristics, MRI field strength [1.5T], and preprocessing/statistical methods). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (the paper does NOT report a whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast or coordinate-based voxelwise GM results comparing substance users vs controls; analyses focus on global GM ratio and genetic associations rather than voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: none (E5 not applicable; study is not a ROI-only paper, and E6 not applicable). Therefore excluded for failure to meet I3 (no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise GM results).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between non-treatment-seeking cocaine-dependent individuals (stimulant class) and non-drug-using controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts with coordinates for significant clusters (left middle frontal gyrus) and voxelwise correlations, uses a 3.0T scanner, and describes preprocessing/statistical software (VBM8/SPM8/DARTEL). Participant characteristics (age, sex), substance use details, and MRI parameters are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine-dependent (stimulant) participants to controls using whole-cortex ROI analyses across 68 Desikan–Killiany regions (i.e., whole-brain coverage). The paper reports between-group contrasts for grey-matter measures (volume, thickness, area) with statistical testing and multiple-test correction, and provides participant demographics, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FreeSurfer v5.3.0). Results are reported for whole-cortex ROIs in the main text (with effect sizes and corrected results). Therefore it satisfies I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons), I3 (whole-brain between-group contrasts via whole-cortex ROI analysis), I4 (results available in main text/tables/figures), and I5 (reporting of age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing). No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only limited study, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of stimulant (methamphetamine) users versus controls that reports whole-brain vertex-wise analyses (surface-based cortical thickness) with cluster coordinates and participant/MRI details. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (reports whole-brain between-group contrast), I4 (results presented in figures/tables/coordinates), I5 (reports age/sex, substance use details, MRI field strength, and preprocessing software). Inclusion criterion not met: I2 (study assesses cortical thickness rather than GM volume/density/concentration as specified by the meta-analysis inclusion criteria). No exclusion criteria (E5/E6) apply. Because the review requires GM volume/density/concentration measures, and this paper reports surface-based cortical thickness rather than the voxelwise GM volume metrics stipulated, it does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded.

This is an empirical English-language human structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing chronic back pain patients on long-term opioids (n=29) with matched CBP controls (n=29). The paper reports whole-brain VBM results (TFCE, FWE-corrected cluster in dorsal paracingulate cortex with peak coordinates), scanner field strength (3T Siemens Prisma), preprocessing/statistical software (FSL-VBM, SIENAX, FIRST, FreeSurfer), and participant demographics and substance-use characteristics (opioid types, duration, MME, blood concentrations, COMM). Thus it satisfies I2, I3, I4, and I5. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only; is empirical). Full text appears complete. Inclusion is appropriate for a meta-analysis of grey-matter differences in opioid users versus controls.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that compares gray matter (GM) volumes between polysubstance users (n=46) and healthy controls (n=30). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FWE-corrected) and lists significant clusters (thalamus, bilateral temporal lobes, ACC, cerebellum, occipital areas) as well as VOI/coordinate-based results and correlations with years of use. Participant demographics (age, all male), substance use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, VBM8) are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. These features satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for whole-brain GM comparisons across substance users vs controls. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical VBM study comparing cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls that reports whole-brain between-group GM volume contrasts (ANCOVA) with coordinates, cluster sizes, thresholds, and significance. Methods report participant demographics, MRI field strength (4T), preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, VBM5.1), and covariates. Results include whole-brain regression and between-group ANCOVA results identifying reduced GM in CUD (VLPFC, OFC) with voxel/cluster-level statistics. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of structural GM differences in substance users vs controls (stimulants).

The study is an empirical English-language structural MRI study that directly compares grey matter (GM) differences between cannabis users and non-users (within a high-risk cohort) using voxelwise tensor-based morphometry. The authors performed whole-brain TBM analyses comparing GM change in cannabis consumers versus non-consumers and report voxel coordinates and SPM maps; they also supplemented whole-brain results with small-volume corrections (SVC) focused on a priori regions. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM2/SPM5, TBM protocol) are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not an ROI-only paper, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of smokers and controls and reports participant demographics and MRI preprocessing (I2 and I5 satisfied). However, it does not report a qualifying whole-brain between-group contrast of GM volume (voxelwise or coordinate-based) comparing substance users (smokers) vs controls. The analyses focus on brain-age (BAG), polygenic risk score associations, atlas-based regional GM measures and tGMV correlations/mediations, but no whole-brain voxelwise or coordinate table of case-control GM differences is provided in the full text. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (only ROI/region-parcellation and derived BAG measures with no qualifying whole-brain between-group GM contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM contrast); I4 (no coordinate/voxelwise whole-brain between-group results reported).

The study is an empirical structural MRI paper of alcohol use disorder that reports FreeSurfer-derived regional cortical thickness and volumetric features and applies an XGBoost brain-age prediction model. However, it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (nor coordinate tables or voxelwise maps) comparing GM volume/density between substance users and controls. Analyses are based on regional/parcellation features and machine-learning prediction rather than whole-brain voxelwise GM group comparisons. Therefore it meets exclusion E5 (only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). It does report participant age/sex, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (so I5 is met). Inclusion criteria I2, I3, and I4 are not met.

This is an empirical, whole-brain longitudinal structural MRI study of adolescent cannabis use that reports vertex-wise cortical thickness results and provides demographic/MRI details. However, the review’s inclusion criterion I2 specifically requires studies assessing grey matter (GM) volume differences (e.g., volume, density, or concentration). This study reports cortical thickness measures rather than GM volume/density/concentration, so it does not meet I2. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (whole-brain analyses reported), I4 (voxelwise/vertexwise results presented in figures/tables), I5 (participant age/sex and MRI/preprocessing details reported). No exclusion criteria (E5, E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to not meeting I2 (metric mismatch: cortical thickness vs GM volume).

Although this is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study that used voxel-based morphometry to examine gray matter in smokers vs. nonsmokers (I2) and reports voxelwise results (coordinates/figures) and detailed participant/MRI/preprocessing information (I4 and I5), the reported VBM findings focus on genotype × smoking interaction effects (MAOA rs1137070 × smoking) rather than presenting a whole-brain between-group contrast directly comparing substance users (smokers) versus controls. The review’s inclusion criterion I3 requires at least one whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast of substance users versus controls. Because no qualifying whole-brain smokers vs. nonsmokers GM contrast is reported in the main results (only interaction effects are reported), the paper does not meet I3 and therefore must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of alcohol users vs controls that reports GM volume/thickness differences using FreeSurfer (satisfies I2) and provides participant and MRI details including age/sex, abstinence duration, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/statistical software (satisfies I5). However, the study reports lobar/region-based (surface-based parcellation and subcortical ROI) and whole-lobe/whole-brain summary measures rather than voxelwise whole-brain statistical contrasts with stereotactic coordinates. It does not provide coordinate-based, whole-brain voxelwise results or statistical maps required for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only / no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I2, I5. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (no whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrast reported). Exclusion criteria met: E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it does not provide whole-brain GM volume contrasts between substance users and controls. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports ROI/parcellation and network analyses without qualifying whole-brain/voxelwise GM volume between-group contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (reports participant age/sex, substance use characteristics, preprocessing/statistical software). Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (not an empirical MRI study comparing current substance users vs controls on GM volume—it is a prospective study of alcohol-naïve children comparing future initiators vs non-initiators), I3 (does not report at least one whole-brain between-group contrast of substance users vs controls comparing GM volume), I4 (does not provide voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain GM volume contrasts). The full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

Exclusion E5 applied: the study reports ROI-based cortical thickness measures and individualized structural covariance network metrics plus MRS in the dACC, but does not present a qualifying whole-brain voxelwise GM volume (e.g., VBM) between-group contrast. An exploratory surface-based cortical thickness analysis is described but ‘did not survive correction’ and no voxelwise/coordinate whole-brain GM volume results or tables of coordinates are provided. Inclusion I5 is met: participant demographics, MRI field strength (3T), and preprocessing/statistical software (Osprey, Gannet, LCModel, Brain Connectivity Toolbox, MATLAB) are reported. Inclusion criteria not met: I2 (study does not assess GM volume/density/concentration contrasts as required), I3 (no whole-brain between-group GM volume contrast reported), and I4 (no voxelwise coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain GM volume results available). Full text appears complete. Therefore excluded under E5.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study (n=676) examining gray matter (cortical thickness and subcortical volumes) in relation to alcohol consumption. The paper reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer) comparing alcohol consumption groups versus a reference group, with cluster-wise corrected results presented in figures and supplementary tables, satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise reporting. Participant age/sex, MRI field strength (3.0T), preprocessing/software (FreeSurfer, FSL), and statistical methods are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that reports whole-brain GM volume comparisons between young adult male smokers and matched non-smokers. The paper provides voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts (smokers vs. non-smokers and subgroup contrasts) with figures/tables of results, reports participant age and sex (male-only), substance-use metrics (pack-years, FTND), MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM8, DARTEL, DPABI). It is not an ROI-only or non-empirical paper. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric comparisons (amygdala, hippocampus, parahippocampus) extracted from the ABCD dataset and does not present any whole-brain voxelwise or whole-brain GM between-group contrasts. This violates inclusion criterion I3 (whole-brain evidence) and therefore meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only analyses). The paper is an empirical structural MRI study (I2) and reports participant age/sex and related demographics (I5), but lacks qualifying whole-brain results (I3/I4 not met). Full text appears complete.

This study is an empirical, English-language MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients vs controls and reports subcortical and global gray-matter differences, but it does not present any whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts of gray matter (e.g., VBM or other whole-brain GM statistical maps/coordinate tables). Instead, analyses are based on automated segmentation of subcortical ROIs (FIRST) and vertex/surface analyses of those ROIs and global SIENAX gray/white matter volumes. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I3 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (ROI-only/no qualifying whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (empirical MRI GM comparisons) and I5 (reporting of age/sex, substance use characteristics, MRI field strength, and software). Inclusion criterion not met: I3 (whole-brain voxelwise between-group GM contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing chronic smokers (nicotine users) to never-smokers with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (tensor-based morphometry) using SPM5. The paper reports between-group whole-brain contrasts and specific regions/clusters of reduced gray matter in unsuccessful and successful quitters versus never smokers, with results summarized in the main text and Supplementary Table S2. Participant age range, gender recording, MRI field strength (Siemens 1.5T), and preprocessing/statistical software (SPM5, MATLAB) are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I2, I3, I4, I5) and violates no exclusion criteria (no ROI-only or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter between active methamphetamine (stimulant) users and matched controls using both whole-brain voxel-wise VBM and ROI subcortical volumetry. It reports whole-brain between-group VBM contrasts (decreased GMD in frontal regions and increased GMD in putamen) and provides voxelwise results in text/figures. Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, MRI field strength (1.5 T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, SIENAX, FIRST, FNIRT) are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusions and appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I2, I3, I4 and I5, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only nor non-empirical).
